In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PfuMBP, like EcoMBP, is a member of the maltodextrin family, which is a subset of the carbohydrate-binding family 18 of the Carbohydrate-Active enZymes (CAZy) database.
PfuMBP has evolved a unique ligand-binding specificity that allows it to bind oligosaccarides composed of three glucopyranose residues or more, but not shorter oligosaccharids, such as maltose.
the binding of oligosaccharidic substrates to maltodextrin- binding protein from Pyrocococus furiosus is a two-step process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the structure of PfuMBB provides an example of how an MBP may be adapted to bind oligosaccarides composed of more than two sugar units.
PfuMBP has a fold similar to EcoMBP and that it binds oligosaccharids composed of three or greater glucopyranose residues.
the PfuMBP structure provides a structural basis for the recognition of maltotrioses and higher oligosacchari-des.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ligand-binding sites of MBPs from hyperthermophilic organisms have a higher affinity for oligosaccharylides composed of more than three glucopyranose residues.

PfuMBP, which has a very high level of resistance to heat and chemical treatments, has evolved by a combination of factors including the presence of prolines in key positions, a tightly packed hydrophilic core, clusters of hydrophobic isoleucines, and salt-bridges.

PfuMBP has evolved to bind oligosugars that are longer than the minimal substrate for EcoMBP, and this may be related to the high temperatures that are encountered in the habitat of PfuMBPs natural host.
